package_info.package_versions: All versions of affected NetBeans projects (26+ repositories, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: The Octopus Scanner malware targets NetBeans project repositories by injecting malicious code into the build process. This ensures that every JAR artifact produced is backdoored, enabling the malware to propagate through the software supply chain, infect downstream users, and facilitate further compromise by exfiltrating sensitive information and self-propagating to additional projects.

execution_context.file_location: NetBeans project files (build scripts such as build.xml, project configuration files)
required_permissions: filesystem (write access to JAR files and project directories)
network (for potential payload updates or C2 communication)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code modifies the JAR file by injecting a malicious payload into every newly built artifact, resulting in the distribution of backdoored JARs to downstream users.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The build process is altered to inject code that is not part of the legitimate project source, which is a hallmark of supply chain attacks. This hidden modification enables the spread of malware without the developer's knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard build scripts are expected to package only the intended application code. Injecting hidden payloads into build artifacts without user consent or documentation violates the integrity of the software supply chain.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate build scripts may add instrumentation or telemetry, but such additions are always documented, opt-in, and do not introduce hidden, undocumented code.
key_indicators: Modification of JAR files during the build process
Presence of injected class files or resources not present in the project source
Absence of documentation or user notification regarding injected payloads
Altered build scripts (e.g., build.xml) with obfuscated or suspicious code blocks

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when an infected JAR is executed)
execution_context.file_location: Injected class files within the JAR (e.g., additional .class files not present in original source)
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write access to scan and modify other NetBeans projects)
environment_vars (access to environment variables for exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code scans the local filesystem for other NetBeans projects, infects them with the malware payload, and exfiltrates environment information to a remote server, enabling lateral movement and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs self-propagation by searching for and infecting other projects, and exfiltrates sensitive environment data to an external server. These behaviors are not present in legitimate application code and are indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal JAR files should not scan the filesystem for unrelated projects, modify them, or transmit environment data to unknown remote servers. Such actions breach user trust and system security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build tools may scan for projects to assist with development workflows, but never for the purpose of infection or unauthorized data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Filesystem scanning for NetBeans project files (e.g., searching for project.xml or build.xml)
Modification of unrelated project files or directories
Creation of new or altered class files in other project directories
Outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs
Exfiltration of environment variables or project metadata

attack_chain.action: Malware is injected into NetBeans project build scripts or configuration files, modifying the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infected JAR files are produced during the build process, containing the malicious payload.

attack_chain.action: Infected JAR files are distributed to downstream users or included in other projects, spreading the backdoored artifacts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes when the infected JAR is run by end users or developers.

attack_chain.action: Injected code executes at runtime, scanning the local filesystem for other NetBeans projects and infecting them with the malware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further propagation of the malware within the developer's environment and across additional projects.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates environment information and project metadata to a remote attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and can further compromise the environment or use the information for targeted attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts or plugins that modify JAR files to inject additional class files or resources not present in the project source
JAR files containing unexpected or undocumented classes, especially with obfuscated or generic names
Runtime behavior that scans for IDE project files (e.g., searching for NetBeans-specific files like project.xml or build.xml) and modifies them
Unexpected outbound network connections from build artifacts or runtime processes, especially to unrecognized domains or IPs
Creation or modification of files in unrelated NetBeans project directories during JAR execution
file_indicators: NetBeans project files (e.g., build.xml, project.xml) with unauthorized or obfuscated modifications
JAR files with injected classes not present in the original project source (e.g., additional .class files with suspicious names)
Presence of duplicate or suspicious class files in build output directories
Altered timestamps or hashes of build scripts and JAR files compared to known-good versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs during or after build (as identified in threat intelligence feeds or IOCs from the report)
Exfiltration of environment variables or project metadata over HTTP/S or other protocols to unknown endpoints
Unusual network activity originating from build or developer environments, especially during or after JAR execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build pipelines for unauthorized modifications to JAR files and build scripts, scan artifacts for undocumented or suspicious classes, and analyze network traffic from build and runtime environments for connections to unknown or attacker-controlled endpoints. Use binary fingerprinting and file integrity monitoring to detect changes in expected artifact content. Employ behavioral analysis to identify unexpected filesystem scanning or modification of unrelated project files during JAR execution.
